CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain in both knees.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male who presents with bilateral knee pain that began over the weekend while moving boxes up and down basement stairs. He reports that by the end of the day both knees were painful, with equal severity bilaterally. He denies specific injury but notes a history of past knee problems. He attributes the current pain to repetitive activity and the weight of the boxes. He has taken acetaminophen and applied ice with minimal relief. The pain was severe enough to disturb his sleep on Saturday night. He denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and headaches. Patient reports occasional elbow pain but notes this is not out of the ordinary. No other symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (several years ago for polycystic kidney disease)
Hypothyroidism
Arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications (for kidney transplant)
Synthroid (for hypothyroidism)
Acetaminophen (as needed for pain)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient lives with family and recently engaged in repetitive heavy lifting (moving boxes).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: stable, no fever, heart rate and blood pressure normal. Cardiac exam reveals a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable compared to prior exams. Knee exam shows edema and erythema of the right knee; left knee appears normal. Pain to palpation of right knee with decreased range of motion noted.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment with no acute fracture. Lab results show normal white blood cell count and good kidney function.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis with right knee involvement: Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Patient advised to rest. Will consider further imaging and physical therapy referral if symptoms persist.
2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Ordered thyroid panel.
3. Arthritis: Continue current management. Note that NSAIDs are limited due to kidney transplant status. Will reassess in a couple of weeks and refer to physical therapy if needed.
